original_question: How are Herman rings created or destroyed when a rational or transcendental map is perturbed, and what is the structure and size of the parameter sets in natural families for which Herman rings occur?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Conclusion, item 3, with nearby context from item 2 on parameter slices for families with Herman rings.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual intent. It almost paraphrases the open direction in Section 6, item 3: it asks about the creation/destruction of Herman rings under perturbation and about the structure and size of the parameter sets in natural families where Herman rings occur. It also correctly spans both rational and transcendental settings, which is how the paper frames the question.
missing_details: The paper poses this as an open research direction in parameter space, not as a theorem or formal conjecture.

The transcendental setting in the paper is specifically transcendental meromorphic dynamics; throughout the survey, rational maps are analytic self-maps of the Riemann sphere and transcendental meromorphic maps have an essential singularity at infinity.

To make the question fully stand-alone, 'Herman ring' should be defined as a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which some iterate is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus.
The perturbation is meant as variation of parameters inside a natural parameterized family, i.e. creation/destruction 'in parameter space,' not an arbitrary informal perturbation of a single map.
The parameter set should be named explicitly as the locus of parameters for which the corresponding map has a Herman ring.

The question should stay narrowly focused on perturbative mechanisms and parameter loci, and not drift into separate open directions in the same conclusion such as classification of all rational maps with Herman rings, boundary geometry, buried Julia components, or omitted-value conjectures.
No ambient algebraic ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'for sufficiently large m' data are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are dynamical and parameter-space assumptions instead.
refined_question: In a natural parameterized family {f_lambda} of rational maps or transcendental meromorphic maps, how can a Herman ring—that is, a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which some iterate of f_lambda is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus—be created or destroyed as the parameter lambda varies, and what are the structure and size of the parameter locus {lambda : f_lambda has a Herman ring}?
justification: The closest official formulation is the third research direction in Section 6, which asks for the mechanisms by which Herman rings are created or destroyed under perturbation in parameter space and for the structure and size of the corresponding parameter sets. I made the question self-contained by importing the paper’s definition of a Herman ring from Section 1 and by rewriting the parameter-set part as an explicit parameter locus {lambda : f_lambda has a Herman ring}. I kept the scope tight: the paper’s nearby context also mentions parameter slices in families with Herman rings, and earlier sections provide rational and transcendental meromorphic family constructions that explain why the question is naturally phrased family-by-family rather than as a global classification problem.
